newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU fine tunes fining mechanism for ignoring court.
newsitem.headline: EU fine tunes fining mechanism for ignoring court.

text.p: The European Commission, weary of non-application of EU legislation in areas like trade and the environment, on Wednesday agreed a method for setting fines on countries who ignore rulings from the EU court.
Although the EU executive did not discuss specific cases, officials said fines -- made possible by the Maastricht Treaty on European Union -- are expected to be proposed in five cases within a month.

The complicated method for setting the fines takes into account how rich a country is, how much voting weight it had in setting the law in the first place and the seriousness and duration of the infringement.
Officials predicted the first countries to fall foul of the system would be Germany and Italy.
Bonn has failed to follow court rulings on ground water, surface water and bird protection. Rome has ignored two rulings ordering it to apply EU legislation on waste disposal in Campania.
The Commission would propose the fines to the Luxembourg-based Court, which will take a final decision on the fine. The Court could take up to a year to take its decision, EU officials said.
